newsitem.title: USA: Liberty Bancorp ups loan loss provision.
newsitem.headline: Liberty Bancorp ups loan loss provision.

text.p: Liberty Bancorp Inc said on Wednesday its loan loss provision in the third quarter of 1996 rose to $4.3 million from $200,000 in the same quarter last year, reflecting higher loan losses in 1996 and loan growth.
The bank said its loan loss provision for the first nine months of 1996 rose to $19.3 million, up from $16.5 million in the first nine months of 1995.

"Given the increased consumer bankruptcies and other weakened national trends in the consumer loan area and the continuing uncertainty as to the direction of the economy, we began making provisions last year and continue to increase the reserve for loan losses in 1996," Liberty Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Charles Nelson said.
The bank also said its net charge-offs in the quarter were $4.3 million versus $2.8 million in the same quarter last year. Most of these were consumer loans, the bank said.
"We think it is prudent to cover consumer loan charge-offs and strengthen Liberty's overall reserve position," he said.
